fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: Allocation cannot be randomised once the intervention has already been delivered.
Randomisation has been ruled out, so no randomised design is available.

fires_when: allocation_unit is “Groups — sites, teams, areas or caseloads”
message: The intervention is delivered to whole groups, so individuals within them cannot be allocated separately.
Significant barriers to randomisation were identified.
unlock: Check whether a stepped-wedge, waitlist or encouragement design addresses the specific objection — these are often accepted where straightforward randomisation is not.

fires_when: equipoise is “No — the effect is considered established”
message: The effect is considered already established, which makes withholding the intervention hard to justify.
unlock: Document the remaining uncertainty, or move to a design that withholds nothing.

message: Stakeholders disagree about whether the effect is already established.
unlock: Resolve this before an ethics application, since it is the usual ground for refusal.

fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: Allocation cannot be randomised once the intervention has already been delivered.
Randomisation has been ruled out, so no randomised design is available.
The intervention is delivered to individuals, so there are no natural clusters to allocate.
Fewer than about 15 clusters. Precision in a cluster design is governed by the number of clusters, so a large number of individuals within them does not compensate.
unlock: Establish whether more clusters can be recruited, or whether individual allocation is possible after all.

message: Significant barriers to randomisation were identified.
unlock: Check whether randomising the order of a phased rollout is acceptable instead.

fires_when: cluster_count is one of “Roughly 15 to 40” or “Fewer than 15”
message: A cluster design needs an intracluster correlation estimate to size properly. With this few clusters the result is sensitive to the value assumed, so take a range to your statistician rather than a single figure.

fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: The rollout order cannot be randomised once delivery has happened.

fires_when: rollout_order_controllable is “No — the order is fixed or externally determined”
message: The rollout order is fixed or externally determined, so there is nothing left to randomise.

fires_when: rollout_order_controllable is “Partly — some influence over sequencing”
message: Only partial influence over the sequencing of the rollout.
unlock: Establish which part of the order is genuinely open. Randomising even a subset of the sequence can be enough.

message: Too few clusters to allocate across a useful number of steps.
unlock: Establish whether more sites can join, or whether fewer, larger steps would work.

fires_when: rollout_order_controllable is not “No — the order is fixed or externally determined”
message: In a stepped-wedge design every unit is treated later in the study than it is untreated, so the treatment effect is entangled with any underlying time trend. The analysis must adjust for time.

fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: Allocation cannot be randomised once the intervention has already been delivered.

fires_when: outcome_reversible is “No — effects persist or accumulate”
message: The outcome does not return to baseline, so a participant cannot serve as their own control in a later period.
Without a washout period the first condition contaminates the second.
Whether the effect persists has not been established.
unlock: Check the evidence on how long the effect lasts; this determines both whether a crossover is possible and how long the washout must be.

message: The feasibility of a washout period has not been established.
unlock: Establish the minimum gap needed, then whether delivery can accommodate it.

fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: Allocation cannot be randomised once the intervention has already been delivered.

fires_when: delay_acceptable is “No — delay is not acceptable”
message: A waitlist design requires part of the group to receive the intervention later.
Whether a delay is acceptable has not been settled.
unlock: Agree the maximum tolerable wait with delivery colleagues. That wait is also the window in which the effect must be measured.

fires_when: delay_acceptable is “Yes — a delay is tolerable”
message: The comparison exists only until the waitlist group is treated, so the design measures a short-run effect. Outcomes that take longer to emerge cannot be captured this way.

fires_when: prospective is “No — the intervention has already been delivered or allocated”
message: The encouragement cannot be randomised once the intervention has been delivered.
No credible way to encourage take-up without assigning the intervention itself, which is what this design requires.
A possible encouragement has been identified but not established.
unlock: Check that it moves take-up appreciably. A weak encouragement yields an estimate for too few people to be useful.

fires_when: exclusion_restriction is one of “Doubtful — plausible alternative routes exist” or “Not yet considered”
message: The encouragement must affect the outcome only by changing take-up. If it carries information or incentive that acts directly, the complier estimate is biased.
unlock: Set out why the encouragement has no direct route to the outcome. This cannot be tested, so it has to be argued.

message: This estimates the effect for those whose take-up the encouragement changed, not for everyone. Those people may differ from the population the decision is about.
A discontinuity design requires assignment by a score, date or threshold.

fires_when: threshold_enforced is “Mostly — the cutoff shifts the probability of treatment”
message: The cutoff shifts the probability of treatment rather than determining it, which is a fuzzy design rather than a sharp one.

fires_when: threshold_manipulation is “Sorting is likely or demonstrated”
message: Sorting around the cutoff means those either side differ in ways beyond treatment, which removes the basis for the comparison.
Whether people can position themselves around the cutoff has not been tested.
unlock: Run a density test for bunching at the cutoff, and check whether those it affects could know the rule and act on it.

message: How strictly the cutoff is applied in practice has not been established.
unlock: Examine administrative records to see how often the rule was overridden. This decides between a sharp and a fuzzy design.

message: Few observations fall near the cutoff, and only those identify the effect. A large total sample does not help.
unlock: Count observations within a plausible bandwidth rather than in the dataset as a whole, and take that figure to a power calculation.

fires_when: assignment_threshold is “Yes — a documented cutoff exists”
message: The estimate depends on the bandwidth chosen around the cutoff. Report results across a range of bandwidths rather than only the one that was selected.

fires_when: assignment_threshold is “Yes — a documented cutoff exists”
message: The result applies at the cutoff. It says little about people far from it, who may be the group the decision concerns.
A discontinuity design requires assignment by a score, date or threshold.

fires_when: threshold_manipulation is “Sorting is likely or demonstrated”
message: Sorting around the cutoff removes the basis for the comparison.
Whether people can position themselves around the cutoff has not been tested.
unlock: Run a density test for bunching at the cutoff.

fires_when: instrument_strength is one of “Weakly” or “Not yet established”
message: A fuzzy design relies on a clear jump in the probability of treatment at the cutoff. A small jump identifies the effect for very few people.
unlock: Estimate the size of the jump in take-up at the cutoff before committing.

message: Few observations near the cutoff, and a fuzzy design needs more than a sharp one.
unlock: Count observations within a plausible bandwidth and power on that figure.

message: This estimates the effect for those at the cutoff whose treatment the rule actually changed — a narrower group than a sharp design addresses.
No factor identified that shifts take-up without affecting the outcome by any other route.

fires_when: exclusion_restriction is “Doubtful — plausible alternative routes exist”
message: Plausible alternative routes from the instrument to the outcome were identified. The exclusion restriction is the whole basis of the design, so this blocks it rather than qualifying it.
A candidate instrument has been identified but not established.
unlock: Check that it predicts take-up, and set out why it cannot affect the outcome directly.

message: The exclusion restriction has not yet been considered.
unlock: Write down every route by which the instrument could reach the outcome, and argue each one away. This cannot be tested statistically.

message: A weak instrument gives estimates that are biased towards the unadjusted association and confidence intervals that understate uncertainty.
unlock: Report first-stage strength. The conventional F above 10 is a rule of thumb that recent work shows is not sufficient for valid inference, so treat it as a floor rather than a target.

message: The strength of the instrument has not been established.
unlock: Estimate the first stage before committing to the design.

message: A difference-in-differences comparison requires outcome data from before the intervention.
No comparison group that did not receive the intervention.

fires_when: parallel_trends_evidence is “No — the trends clearly diverge”
message: The groups were already moving apart before the intervention, so the difference afterwards cannot be attributed to it.

fires_when: staggered_rollout is one of “Yes — adoption was staggered” or “Planned but not yet begun”
message: Adoption is or will be staggered, so this is not a two-period comparison. The staggered-adoption design applies instead.
With one pre-period the parallel-trends assumption cannot be examined at all. It would be assumed rather than supported.
unlock: Find at least two further pre-periods so the trends can be compared.

message: Whether the groups moved together before the intervention has not been examined.
unlock: Plot both series across every available pre-period. This is the main thing a reviewer will look for.

message: A possible comparison group has been identified but its comparability is not established.
unlock: Check that it faced comparable conditions and was not affected by the intervention itself.

message: A difference-in-differences comparison requires outcome data from before the intervention.
No comparison group that did not receive the intervention.

fires_when: staggered_rollout is “No — a single common start date”
message: All units started at the same time, so there is no variation in timing. The two-period design applies instead.

fires_when: parallel_trends_evidence is “No — the trends clearly diverge”
message: The groups were already moving apart before the intervention.
Whether the groups moved together before the intervention has not been examined.
unlock: Compare trends for each adoption cohort separately, not just in aggregate — a single cohort can mask divergence in another.

fires_when: staggered_rollout is “Planned but not yet begun”
message: The staggered rollout is planned but has not begun.
unlock: If the order is still open, randomising it gives a stepped-wedge design at Tier 1 for no additional data cost.

fires_when: staggered_rollout is one of “Yes — adoption was staggered” or “Planned but not yet begun”
message: Under staggered adoption the conventional two-way fixed effects estimator averages comparisons that include already-treated units acting as controls, and can place negative weights on some of them. Use an estimator built for staggered timing — Callaway-Sant'Anna, Sun-Abraham or Borusyak-Jaravel-Spiess. This is an estimator choice; it does not change the tier.

fires_when: pre_periods is one of “None” or “One period only”
message: A synthetic control is built by matching the treated unit's pre-intervention path, which requires a run of periods rather than one.
No untreated units available to weight into a comparison.
A short pre-period gives the weighting little to match on, so good pre-period fit may be achieved by chance rather than by genuine similarity.
unlock: Extend the pre-period if the data allow. Where it cannot be extended, the augmented estimator corrects some of the resulting bias.

fires_when: donor_pool is “A few, of uncertain comparability”
message: Few candidate donor units, of uncertain comparability.
unlock: Check that donors were not themselves affected by the intervention, and that none experienced its own shock during the period.

message: Conventional confidence intervals do not apply. Inference is by placebo tests across the donor pool, which is why pool size affects what can be concluded as well as how well the method fits.
No equivalent series for an unaffected group. Without one this is a single interrupted time series at Tier 5.
A pre-intervention trend must be estimable on both series.
The interruption point must be known to separate before from after.
A possible control series has been identified but not established.
unlock: Check it was genuinely unaffected by the intervention and is subject to the same external influences.

fires_when: time_points is “Fewer than four each side”
message: Too few time points to estimate a trend on each side of the interruption with any confidence.
unlock: Aim for roughly eight points per segment. This is a working convention rather than a derived minimum.
threshold: 8 time points per segment (range 6–12) — convention · contested

message: Other changes coincided with the intervention. A control series helps only where it was exposed to those same changes.
unlock: Establish whether the control series was affected by the same coinciding changes.

message: Whether anything else changed at the same time has not been checked.
unlock: Compile a timeline of other policy and funding changes across the study period.

message: This design compares either side of a date, so the date must be known precisely.
No data from before the change.
Other changes occurred at the same date. With no comparison group there is nothing to separate their effect from the intervention's.

fires_when: time_points is “Fewer than four each side”
message: This design estimates locally either side of the date, so it needs observations close to it. With very few time points there is nothing to fit a local comparison to, and a plain interrupted time series over the whole series is the available design instead.

fires_when: time_points is “Roughly four to eight each side”
message: Local estimation around the date rests on the observations nearest it, which are fewer than the length of the series suggests.
unlock: Count the observations within a plausible window either side of the date rather than across the whole series, and power on that figure.

message: The date is approximate or the change was phased, which blurs the discontinuity.
unlock: Establish a precise date. Where the change was genuinely phased, a design built on the phasing is likely to serve better.

message: Whether anything else changed at the same date has not been checked.
unlock: Compile a timeline around the date. This is the main threat to the design, so it needs doing before committing to it.

message: Placed at Tier 3 rather than Tier 2: continuity across a date is a claim that nothing else changed then, which is a time-series argument rather than local randomisation. Some sources place it higher where the cutoff is externally imposed.
Matching can only adjust for what is measured. With little covariate data there is nothing to match on.

fires_when: overlap is “Poor — the groups barely overlap”
message: Where treated and untreated units barely resemble each other there are no comparable pairs to form.

fires_when: overlap is “Limited — overlap only in part of the range”
message: Overlap exists only across part of the range, so any estimate applies to that part and not to the whole population.
unlock: Define the region of common support and state that the result applies there. Weighting handles limited overlap better than matching does.

message: Whether the groups overlap has not been examined.
unlock: Compare covariate distributions between treated and untreated units before committing.

fires_when: confounders_measured is “Some known drivers are not measured”
message: Known drivers of selection are not in the data. Matching cannot adjust for them and balance diagnostics will not reveal them.
unlock: Plan a sensitivity analysis quantifying how strong an unmeasured confounder would need to be to overturn the finding.

message: The drivers of who received the intervention have not been established.
unlock: List them first, then check which are measured. The gap between the two lists is the design's main weakness.

message: Covariate data has known gaps.
unlock: Document which variables are missing and why, so reviewers can judge the residual risk.

message: Good balance on measured covariates is not evidence that unmeasured confounding is absent. It shows the matching worked, not that the assumption holds.

fires_when: pre_periods is one of “Several periods” or “Two or three periods”
message: Pre-intervention outcome data is available. Matching on prior outcomes as well as characteristics places this at the upper end of Tier 4, and the Maryland scale allows level 3 where comparability is demonstrated rather than asserted.
Weighting can only adjust for what is measured.

fires_when: overlap is “Poor — the groups barely overlap”
message: Where some units had almost no chance of receiving the intervention, their weights become extreme and the estimate is driven by a handful of observations. This is a positivity violation.

fires_when: overlap is “Limited — overlap only in part of the range”
message: Limited overlap produces large weights that dominate the estimate.
unlock: Use overlap weights or trimming, which target the population where the comparison is actually supported, and report how many observations the weights concentrate on.

message: Whether the groups overlap has not been examined.
unlock: Examine the distribution of estimated propensity scores in both groups before committing; this is what determines whether weighting is viable at all.

fires_when: confounders_measured is “Some known drivers are not measured”
message: Known drivers of selection are not in the data.
unlock: Plan a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

message: The drivers of who received the intervention have not been established.
unlock: List them, then check which are measured.

message: Report the distribution of the weights alongside the estimate. A result resting on a few heavily weighted observations is fragile even where the average looks sound.
Standardisation models the outcome given the covariates, so it needs those covariates to be measured.

fires_when: overlap is “Poor — the groups barely overlap”
message: With no overlap the outcome model would extrapolate into regions where no comparable units exist, which the method cannot signal.

fires_when: confounders_measured is “Some known drivers are not measured”
message: Known drivers of selection are not in the data.
unlock: Plan a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

message: The drivers of who received the intervention have not been established.
unlock: List them, then check which are measured.

message: Overlap has not been examined, and extrapolation beyond it is silent here.
unlock: Check overlap even though this method does not require it as directly as matching, because the model will extrapolate without warning.

message: The estimate depends on the outcome model being correctly specified. A doubly-robust estimator gives a second chance: it remains consistent if either the outcome model or the treatment model is right.

fires_when: time_varying_confounding is “No — treatment is a one-off”
message: Treatment is a one-off, so conventional adjustment is appropriate and simpler. The g-methods exist for feedback between treatment and confounders.
Modelling the feedback between treatment and confounders requires repeated measures of both.
The time-varying confounders must themselves be measured.
Whether treatment affects later confounders has not been established.
unlock: Draw the causal structure over time. If no arrow runs from treatment to a later confounder, a simpler design will serve.

fires_when: confounders_measured is “Some known drivers are not measured”
message: Known drivers of selection are not in the data. The g-methods address confounding by measured time-varying factors; they do nothing about unmeasured ones.
unlock: Plan a sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding.

fires_when: time_varying_confounding is “Yes — treatment and confounders evolve together”
message: Where treatment affects later confounders, adjusting for them conventionally blocks part of the effect, while omitting them leaves confounding. Both directions are wrong, which is why a g-method is needed rather than preferred.
The whole design rests on estimating the pre-intervention trend, so pre-period data is required.
The interruption point must be known.
Other changes coincided with the intervention. With no comparison group there is nothing to distinguish their effect from the intervention's.

fires_when: time_points is “Fewer than four each side”
message: Too few time points to estimate a trend on each side of the interruption.
unlock: Aim for roughly eight points per segment. A working convention rather than a derived minimum, so treat it as a range.
threshold: 8 time points per segment (range 6–12) — convention · contested

fires_when: time_points is “Roughly four to eight each side”
message: Enough points to fit a model, but not enough to characterise the trend confidently.
unlock: Extend the series if the data allow, and report the estimate's sensitivity to the window chosen.

fires_when: autocorrelation_plan is one of “No” or “Not yet decided”
message: Adjacent time points resemble each other. Ignoring this makes the effect appear more precisely estimated than it is.
unlock: Test for autocorrelation and model it, or use an estimator that accounts for it.

message: Whether anything else changed at the same time has not been checked.
unlock: Compile a timeline of other changes across the study period. Without a comparison group this is the design's central vulnerability.

message: Nothing here can test whether the pre-intervention trend would have continued. If a control series can be found the design moves to Tier 3 for no extra data on the treated unit.
Contribution analysis tests a stated theory of change. Without one there is no claim to assess.
unlock: Develop a theory of change with delivery staff and stakeholders. That work is part of the evaluation rather than a prerequisite for it.

message: The theory of change is still in development.
unlock: Finalise the causal chain and the assumptions at each link before gathering evidence against it.

message: Evidence for the steps in the causal chain is patchy.
unlock: Identify which links are least evidenced; those determine what can be concluded.

message: The output is confidence in a contribution claim, not an effect size. Where a number is needed for a business case, this will not produce one.
Realist evaluation works by eliciting mechanisms from those who deliver and receive the intervention. Without access to them the method has no input.
Limited access to the people involved in delivery.
unlock: Establish which groups can be reached. Partial access narrows which context-mechanism-outcome configurations can be examined rather than ruling the method out.

message: Findings are explicitly about what works for whom in which context. They do not generalise in the way an average effect is assumed to.
Process tracing tests a causal pathway step by step against evidence. Without documentation of those steps there is nothing to trace.
Documentation covers only part of the hypothesised pathway.
unlock: Identify which steps lack evidence. A pathway can still be assessed where the gaps are at links that carry less of the argument.

message: There is no stated pathway to trace.
unlock: Set out the hypothesised causal chain before gathering evidence against it.

message: Conclusions apply within the case examined. Establishing that a mechanism operated here is not evidence about how often it operates elsewhere.
